22. Case study: drug utilisation

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-22-case-drug.Rmd
book-22-case-drug.Rmd

What you will learn

Separate an ATC-class definition from an ingredient study, define new users, and measure covered days, persistence and discontinuation.

You need: the installed packages and practice resources, concept discovery, and the preceding tutorial chapters. Run these sections in order in a fresh book-work session. All observations are public synthetic teaching data; the numerical results are not clinical evidence.

Research question and vocabulary feasibility

For a prespecified ATC class, what fraction of the first treatment year is covered, and when does the first treatment era end? First establish that the vocabulary supports that class. The small GiBleed vocabulary has no ATC entries; an ATC-class estimate is therefore unavailable on this practice resource. The executable worked ATC analysis therefore uses a separate, explicitly synthetic catalogue and longitudinal supply histories. A subsequent celecoxib ingredient example shows why the unmodified GiBleed records cannot support an adherence conclusion.

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
source("tools/book/case-helpers.R")
practice <- book_connect("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns
atc <- ds.omop.concept.search(NULL, vocabulary = "ATC", standard_only = FALSE, conns = conns)$pooled
print(data.frame(ATC_classes_available = NROW(atc)))
#>   ATC_classes_available
#> 1                     0

On an ATC-enabled resource, search the intended class with standard_only = FALSE, inspect its class level and descendants, check prevalence, then save that set. Do not infer an ATC hierarchy from a drug’s spelling.

Run the ATC-class selection on the teaching catalogue

The category chapter’s synthetic catalogue lets us execute the class-selection workflow without pretending that GiBleed contains an ATC hierarchy. The class, its descendant medicine and its exposure records are all explicitly synthetic. Six people follow each of three invented supply patterns, indexed at day zero:

Pattern Fill days Days supplied per fill
Continuous, with early refills 0, 100, 220 120, 120, 125
Two overlapping fills, then stop 0, 30 60, 60
Short course, then restart 0, 120 30, 30

Each has a complete observed year. Supply carried forward from early refills counts once; a restart after a gap over 30 days starts a new era. These public patterns let us predict the results before looking at protected summaries.

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
DSI::datashield.logout(conns)
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
class_practice <- book_fixture(categories = TRUE, drug_histories = TRUE, symbol = "class_omop")
class_conns <- class_practice$conns
classes <- ds.omop.concept.search(NULL, vocabulary = "ATC", standard_only = FALSE,
  conns = class_conns, symbol = "class_omop")$pooled
knitr::kable(classes[c("concept_name", "concept_class_id", "standard_concept")])
concept_name concept_class_id standard_concept
Teaching ATC first level ATC 1st C
Teaching ATC second level ATC 2nd C 
class_id <- classes$concept_id[classes$concept_class_id == "ATC 2nd"]
knitr::kable(ds.omop.concept.descendants(class_id, conns = class_conns, symbol = "class_omop")$pooled)
concept_id concept_name domain_id vocabulary_id min_levels_of_separation
950001 Practice medicine Drug Fixture 1 
knitr::kable(ds.omop.concept.prevalence("drug_exposure", scope = "pooled", conns = class_conns, symbol = "class_omop")$pooled)
concept_id n_persons concept_name
950001 15 Practice medicine 
class_set <- omop_concept_set(class_id, descendants = TRUE)
class_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(class_set, class_file)

A classification concept groups descendants; it is not a standard ingredient substitution through Maps to. The descendant list establishes the selected medicine before the protected inventory establishes its use. The prevalence entry is a disclosure-controlled count band (15 here), not the exact cohort size. The subsequent admitted analysis summary reports 18 valid people; use that analysis denominator when interpreting its mean.

class_users <- omop_new_users(class_set, washout_days = 365)
class_users$filters <- c(class_users$filters, list(omop_observed(after = 364)))
class_drug <- omop_event("drug_exposure", class_set)
class_era <- omop_era(class_drug, gap = 30, by = "ingredient", stockpile = TRUE)
class_days <- omop_variable(event = class_era, reducer = omop_reduce("covered_days",
  window = omop_window(0, 364), coverage = "effective_supply"))
class_persistence <- omop_variable(event = class_era,
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_era_days", window = omop_window(0, 364)))
class_study <- omop_study(class_users, outputs = "baseline", baseline = list(
  covered = class_days, persistence = class_persistence,
  discontinued = omop_number_flag(class_persistence, "lt", 365),
  pdc = omop_number_derive(list(days = class_days),
    book_expr(book_op("/", book_col("days"), book_lit(365))), unit = "1")))
class_result <- recipe_execute(class_study, out = c(baseline = "D_class_use"), conns = class_conns, symbol = "class_omop")
class_pdc <- dsBaseClient::ds.mean("D_class_use$pdc", type = "combine", datasources = class_conns)
class_pdc$Global.Mean
#>                 EstimatedMean Nmissing Nvalid Ntotal
#> studiesCombined     0.4977169        0     18     18

The expected covered days are 365, 120 and 60. Their mean PDC is (365 + 120 + 60) / (3 × 365), about 0.498. First-era persistence is 365, 120 and 30 days: the restarted course adds covered days but does not extend the first era. Two of the three patterns meet the protocol’s first-era discontinuation rule. Recorded supply is not proof of ingestion or permanent cessation. The class has one ingredient; a protocol with several ingredients must decide whether switching still counts as persistence on the class.

knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_class_use$covered",

The summary spans 60 to 365 covered days, consistent with the declared patterns. Keep this connection for the persistence and discontinuation exercises. Next, inspect the unmodified GiBleed ingredient records and their decisive limitation.

conns <- practice$conns

drug_set <- omop_concept_set(ingredient_id, descendants = TRUE)

Define new users and the denominator

Require a 365-day washout and a complete next year of observation. This complete- follow-up restriction simplifies the demonstration but can select healthier or more stable patients. A real protocol may instead use each person’s observed time.

users <- omop_new_users(drug_set, washout_days = 365)
users$filters <- c(users$filters, list(omop_observed(after = 364)))
drug <- omop_event("drug_exposure", drug_set)
era <- omop_era(drug, gap = 30, by = "ingredient", stockpile = TRUE)
covered <- omop_variable(event = era, reducer = omop_reduce("covered_days",
  window = omop_window(0, 364), coverage = "effective_supply"))
persistence <- omop_variable(event = era, reducer = omop_reduce("first_era_days",
  window = omop_window(0, 364)))
utilisation <- omop_study(users, outputs = "baseline", baseline = list(
  covered = covered, persistence = persistence,
  pdc = omop_number_derive(list(covered = covered),
    book_expr(book_op("/", book_col("covered"), book_lit(365))), unit = "1"),
  discontinued = omop_number_flag(persistence, "lt", 365),
  fills = omop_variable(event = drug, reducer = omop_reduce("count", window = omop_window(0, 364)))))
book_symbols(recipe_execute(utilisation, out = c(baseline = "D_utilisation"), conns = conns))
#>        baseline 
#> "D_utilisation"
knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_utilisation$covered", datasources = conns)))
Site Statistic Value
site 5% 1
site 10% 1
site 25% 1
site 50% 1
site 75% 1
site 90% 1
site 95% 1
site Mean 1

Every released GiBleed covered-days summary is one day. The public input has one celecoxib exposure per person, zero days_supply, and equal start/end dates: only the inclusive one-day recorded span is available. It cannot establish longitudinal supply, adherence, restarts or actual treatment discontinuation.

The stockpiled era carries overlapping supply forward when that information exists, as in the synthetic ATC example. Covered days count the union of effective supply days, avoiding double counting overlap. Era persistence tolerates a declared 30-day gap; it is not the same as covered days. Recorded prescribing is not proof of actual ingestion.

PDC and discontinuation

Proportion of days covered (PDC) divides covered days by the 365 eligible days. The native expression declares a dimensionless result (unit = "1"), rather than retaining the covered-days coordinate after a display rescaling. A first era shorter than 365 days is a protocol-defined discontinuation indicator under this gap rule, not proof of permanent treatment cessation.

book_symbols(recipe_execute(utilisation, out = c(baseline = "D_utilisation_analysis"), conns = conns))
#>                 baseline 
#> "D_utilisation_analysis"
knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_utilisation_analysis$pdc", datasources = conns)))
Site Statistic Value
site 5% 0.0027397
site 10% 0.0027397
site 25% 0.0027397
site 50% 0.0027397
site 75% 0.0027397
site 90% 0.0027397
site 95% 0.0027397
site Mean 0.0027397

Here every GiBleed PDC is 1/365 (about 0.00274), solely because of the one-day recording pattern. This is arithmetic on the available record, not a clinical adherence estimate. The synthetic ATC example supplies the longitudinal teaching comparison.

Inspect the definition before interpreting these values. Changing stockpiling, gap tolerance or the follow-up denominator changes the question even when the column name remains PDC. Privacy checks still apply to the final table and releases.

Exercises

1. Summarise persistence in both resources. Compare its units with PDC and explain why only the synthetic example demonstrates varied supply histories.

Solution 1

knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_utilisation_analysis$persistence", datasources = conns)))
Site Statistic Value

knitr::kable(book_summary(dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_class_use$persistence", datasources = class_conns)))
Site Statistic Value
site 5% 30.0000
site 10% 30.0000
site 25% 30.0000
site 50% 120.0000
site 75% 365.0000
site 90% 365.0000
site 95% 365.0000
site Mean 171.6667

GiBleed persistence is uniformly one recorded day. Synthetic first-era persistence ranges from 30 to 365 days, with a mean of (365 + 120 + 30)/3 = 171.67 days. Persistence is measured in days; PDC is a fraction. A tolerated gap contributes to an era’s span but need not contribute covered supply days.

2. Count the discontinuation indicator in both resources and interpret it.

Solution 2

knitr::kable(book_counts(dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_utilisation_analysis$discontinued", datasources = conns)))
Category Count
1 1745
NA 0 
knitr::kable(book_counts(dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_class_use$discontinued", datasources = class_conns)))
Category Count
0 6
1 12
NA 0

All 1,745 GiBleed people have an indicator of one because the available record ends on its start date; this does not establish clinical discontinuation. The synthetic example has 12 indicators of one and six of zero, as predicted from the supply patterns. The indicator refers to the first era; restarting remains possible and is explicitly present in the third synthetic pattern.

3. Save the ingredient definition. Would changing its name to an ATC code turn this into an ATC-class analysis?

Solution 3

set_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(drug_set, set_file)
identical(readRDS(set_file), drug_set)
#> [1] TRUE

No. Class membership comes from the vocabulary hierarchy, not the local label.

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = class_conns, symbol = "class_omop")
DSI::datashield.logout(class_conns)
unlink(class_practice$path)

Recap

Check vocabulary and supply-history feasibility first. The synthetic ATC example shows continuous supply, overlap and restarting. GiBleed supports ingredient selection but its one-day records cannot establish adherence. Distinguish covered supply, era persistence, PDC and protocol-defined discontinuation, and state the denominator and follow-up selection explicitly.
